name: Sickle Cell-Beta-Thalassemia Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Hematologic and Molecular Diagnostic Criteria for Sickle Cell-Beta-Thalassemia

criteria.description: Presence of HbS and reduced or absent HbA on hemoglobin electrophoresis consistent with sickle cell-beta-thalassemia
Identification of pathogenic mutations in both HBB gene alleles: one causing sickle cell mutation and one causing beta-thalassemia mutation
Clinical manifestations consistent with sickling and hemolytic anemia such as vaso-occlusive crises and chronic anemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Detection of HbS and beta-thalassemia mutations by hemoglobin electrophoresis and genetic testing with supportive clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires differentiation from sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia trait; molecular testing is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sickled erythrocytes on peripheral blood smear

searchTerms: long-term destruction of red blood cells
chronic anemia from red cell breakdown

pathognomonic.symptomName: Vaso-occlusive crises with ischemic pain episodes

searchTerms: yellowing of skin from high bilirubin
jaundice caused by red cell breakdown
chronic fatigue due to low red blood cells

common.symptomName: Frequent infections due to functional asplenia
searchTerms: frequent infections due to spleen not working

occasional.symptomName: Avascular necrosis of femoral or humeral heads
searchTerms: bone death in hip or shoulder
avascular necrosis of femur or humerus
loss of blood supply causing bone damage
gallstones caused by chronic red cell breakdown
brain blood flow blockage causing stroke

laboratory: Hemoglobin electrophoresis showing HbS and reduced or absent HbA
Peripheral blood smear with sickled red blood cells and anisopoikilocytosis
Elevated indirect bilirubin and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH)
imaging: MRI showing avascular necrosis of bone
Transcranial Doppler ultrasound for stroke risk assessment
genetic: Molecular genetic testing confirming HBB gene mutations: one sickle cell mutation (Glu6Val) and one beta-thalassemia mutation
other: Functional asplenia demonstrated by Howell-Jolly bodies on blood smear

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of homozygous HbS without beta-thalassemia mutation
More severe hemolytic anemia and earlier onset
Different hemoglobin electrophoresis pattern with absent HbA
Severe anemia with absent or very low HbA
Different clinical course with transfusion dependence

redFlags: Acute chest syndrome presenting with respiratory distress
Sudden onset of focal neurological deficits suggesting stroke
Severe anemia with rapid hemoglobin drop indicating aplastic crisis
references: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute. Evidence-Based Management of Sickle Cell Disease. 2014.
Hoffman R, et al. Hematology: Basic Principles and Practice. 7th Edition. 2018.
